parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks a federal universal-exposure layer on a division already in the worst legal-risk group. The 2025 executive order and 2025 Supreme Court ruling fix passport markers to assigned sex, bar X markers, and document confiscation/stranding; the February 2025 cable directs refusal where sex is doubted and invites fraud/lifetime-ineligibility findings — a border exposure reaching every outed visitor. Eight-plus foreign governments issued travel advisories. Locally, gender-identity civil-rights protection was repealed (July 2025) with local stronger ordinances barred, and the 2023 school rule binds visitors on school grounds by birth certificate. Immigration-custody abuse of trans detainees is documented. Mitigants: no criminalisation of identity, no credible execution path, hate-crime statute, some orders enjoined, violence data unusable (undercount).

entry_documents.exposure: Executive order plus Nov 2025 Supreme Court ruling fix passport/visa markers to sex assigned at birth; X markers barred; travellers report passports confiscated or blocked and being stranded; Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse on sex doubt and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, with limited waiver; ACLU suit unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can escalate into fraud allegation → refusal or detention, interacting with custody exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Transgender men in immigration custody reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse with guards invoking their gender presentation; federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for trans inmates (hair, hormones, drugs).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some executive orders blocked or enjoined; legal-aid FAQ guides documentation strategy.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor refused entry or flagged for sex misrepresentation can enter this custody system.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: School-grounds rule (2023) requires everyone including visitors to use birth-certificate restrooms; equality map lists this division among enacted facility bans; 2025 statute defines sex unchangeably; a restroom arrest with 24-hour hold in the men's ward occurred elsewhere nationally, showing the pattern's real escalation.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No documented non-school adult public-restroom statute; single-person facilities exist in schools (guardian-consent framing for students).
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility rule plus repealed civil-rights law means ejection or trespass charge has no state-law remedy.

care_services.exposure: Division's top court's 2019 surgery-coverage protection rests on a civil-rights statute from which gender identity was removed in 2025; national care restrictions and subpoenas of youth patient records affect climate.
care_services.protection: Litigation kept adult surgery coverage available; adult care not otherwise barred.
care_services.interaction: Repeal removes the statutory hook future coverage litigation relied on.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official framing: 'gender ideology' as extremist-adjacent in reward memo and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy; 'chemical and surgical mutilation' order; prosecution directive against teachers facilitating social transition; first known bathroom arrest described as deliberate cruelty.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism document states powers will not target mere disagreement; reward is not conditioned on gender ideology.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Heightened official framing raises probability of hostile encounters at any outing.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling parent/child face school-grounds birth-certificate rule; solo minors affected by federal hostility framing; gender-affirming care banned for minors in 27 units nationally and nationally in this division's 2023 law; single-person facility option written as student-plus-guardian-consent.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented prosecution of visiting parents for a child's presentation.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family outings to schools/campuses place a minor directly under the visitor-binding rule.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific homicide figures; monitoring analysis states all counts are undercount floors, so neither safety nor danger is established; legal-risk grade predicts official behaviour, not private violence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 23 units cover it in state bias statutes (this division's status unclear); no sodomy law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Private violence risk remains an open question, weighted lightly.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Gender identity removed from state civil-rights statutes (July 2025) and stronger local ordinances barred (2026): no state remedy for service, housing or job discrimination; division listed in worst legal-risk group July 2026; several federal orders unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: 2020 national employment ruling and national hate-crime statute on the books; some orders enjoined; civil-liberties FAQ and ongoing litigation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper federal protections are precisely what the executive orders target, so recourse is uncertain rather than absent.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's register excludes transgender visitors routinely with no real appeal. Here exclusion is not automatic: entry is often possible, the fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic, and litigation is live — so somewhat above 0.35-A, though passport confiscation/stranding and directive refusal on sex doubt make the border layer comparable in kind.

Kestrel Isles offers secondary screening with administrative refusal and slow remedies, but no criminal exposure and no facility or custody harm. This dossier adds a fraud/lifetime-ineligibility lever, visitor-binding birth-certificate facility rules, custody abuse records, and repealed civil-rights protection — materially below 0.55-B.

Meridia's trained, respectful border practice with working tribunal remedies sits far above: here the state itself restricts markers, instructs refusal on sex doubt, and the division strips discrimination remedies — clear separation, this rating well below 0.75-C.

Closest fit: routine universal identity exposure at checkpoints and services, documented detention/humiliation and denial of protections, scarce remedies, inconsistent enforcement, and no credible imprisonment or execution pathway for visitors.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system is federal document and entry control layered over a division that repealed its own protections. Every trans visitor carries the passport-marker regime (M/F only, markers fixed to assigned sex, upheld November 2025) and the February 2025 cable's refusal-plus-fraud logic — a universal exposure whose severity runs from secondary screening to refusal, stranding, or lifetime ineligibility, though it is never automatic and is litigated. Locally the exposure is exclusion rather than punishment: the visitor-binding school birth-certificate rule, an enacted facility ban, no state discrimination remedy after the July 2025 repeal, and 2026 preemption of stronger city ordinances. Escalation potential is shown nationally by a restroom arrest with a men's-ward hold and by documented trans-specific abuse in immigration custody. Counterweights are real but partial: no criminalisation of identity, no credible execution path, a national hate-crime statute, some orders enjoined, and violence data that cannot be used either way. This sits in Elevated Risk, above routine secondary-screening anchors, well below acceptance-with-working-remedies.
